2024:</subfield><subfield code="b">Hasbani River (The Hasbani (Arabic: الحاصباني = al-Ḥāṣbānī; Hebrew: חצבני = Ḥatzbaní) or Snir Stream (Hebrew: נחל שניר = Naḥal Śenir), is the major tributary of the Jordan River. Native people in the mid-19th century knew the Hasbani as the Upper Jordan River; The Hasbani runs for 25 mi (40 km) through the Wadi al-Taym in Lebanon before crossing the border at Ghajar and shortly after joining with the Banias and Dan Rivers at a point in northern Israel, to form the River Jordan. For about 4 km (2.5 mi) downstream of Ghajar, the Hasbani forms the border between Lebanon and the Golan Heights; The Hasbani River derives most of its discharge from two springs in Lebanon, the Wazzani and the Haqzbieh, the latter being a group of springs on the uppermost Hasbani)</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="670" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">Britannica online website, July 5, 2024:</subfield><subfield code="b">in article on the Jordan River (Ḥāṣbānī, river, Lebanon; the Ḥāṣbānī, which rises in Lebanon at an elevation of 1,800 feet)</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="670" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">Snir Stream Nature Reserve, via Israel Nature and Parks Authority website, July 5, 2024</subfield><subfield code="b">(the Snir Stream (Hatsbani) is the longest of the Jordan River tributaries)</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="670" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">Nahal Snir (Hasbani River), via inisrael website, July 5, 2024</subfield><subfield code="b">(Nahal Snir (Hasbani River); Nahal Snir (Hasbani) is the longest in the sources of the Jordan)</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="670" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">Hasbani-Wazzani River, the northern tributary of the shared Jordan River, map, via ResearchGate website, July 5, 2024</subfield><subfield code="b">(Hasbani-Wazzani River)</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="670" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">Shentsis, Isabella. Assessing water withdrawals in scarce-data transboundary areas by use of dynamic precipitation-flow relationships, in Water, v. 13(11), 1440 (2021), viewed online July 8, 2024:</subfield><subfield code="b">p. 2 (The Hasbani River (named Snir in Israel) is one of the major tributaries of the Upper Jordan River)</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="670" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">Inventory of shared water resources in Western Asia, via WWW, July 8, 2024:</subfield><subfield code="b">Surface water > Jordan River basin (The Jordan River headwaters (Hasbani, Banias and Dan) are fed by groundwater and seasonal surface runoff. The Lower Jordan River originally received its main inflow from the outlet of Lake Tiberias and the Yarmouk River, the largest tributary, as well as from several wadis and aquifers. The flow of the Upper Jordan River into Lake Tiberias remains nearly natural)</subfield><subfield code="u">http://waterinventory.org/surface_water/jordan-river-basin</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="670" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">The Canadian Jewish news, Sept. 24, 2009, viewed via ProQuest, July 8, 2024:</subfield><subfield code="b">p. 10 (Since 2002, Lebanon has been redirecting waters from the Wazzani River to villages in its south. The Wazzani runs into the Hatsbani, which in turn feeds the Jordan River, the Kinneret's largest single source. The Hatsbani provides the Jordan with 25 per cent of its water)</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="670" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">ויקיפדיה, נצפה 26 ינואר 2021</subfield><subfield code="b">(נַחַל שְׂנִיר [ידוע גם בשם חצבני או חצבאני כשמו הערבי] הוא אחד ממקורות הירדן, והארוך מביניהם. רובו של הנחל נמצא בתחומי לבנון, ורק חלקו התחתון, מאזור הכפר ע'ג'ר ועד לנקודת חיבורו עם נחל דן ונחל חרמון ליד קיבוץ שדה נחמיה באצבע הגליל, נמצא בתחום מדינת ישראל. בנקודת המפגש עם הנחלים האחרים הם יוצרים את נהר הירדן. חלק מהנחל בסמוך למעיין ברוך הוא שמורת טבע. הוא אחד הנחלים הארוכים במדינת ישראל.)</subfield><subfield code="u">https://he.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D7%A0%D7%97%D7%9C_%D7%A9%D7%A0%D7%99%D7%A8</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="781" ind1=" " ind2="0"><subfield code="z">Israel</subfield><subfield code="z">Senir River</subfield></datafield><datafield tag="933" ind1=" " ind2=" "><subfield code="a">cnr 202101</subfield></datafield></record>
